subject: SIG-lite / subprocessor ancestry & curated evidence pack
messages:
From: Elena Marsh <elena.marsh@phlexhealth.com>
To: monica.patel@redwood.com
Cc: procure@phlexhealth.com, security@phlexhealth.com
Date: 2027-05-02T09:12:00Z
Subject: SIG-lite request: subprocessor lineage + short evidence set

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo — Phlex is progressing through the security gate for clinical data processing. The security & procurement teams reviewed Redwood’s overview and asked if you can provide a compact SIG-lite response focusing on: (1) an authoritative subprocessor roster with country of processing, (2) KMS ownership boundaries for any customer key material, and (3) a one-page pointer list to CAIQ controls where you rely on upstream cloud providers.

We'd prefer a single ZIP with: a CSV of subprocessors (name, role, data types, processing country), a short PDF index mapping SIG/CAIQ control IDs to evidence artifacts, and any residency attestation you can provide. Our internal deadline for vendor pack submission is EOD May 6.

Two small asks: if any subprocessor is transitive (i.e., your partner uses another vendor), please list that chain up to two hops. Also flag any on-prem or air-gapped integrations that require different handling.

Can you confirm scope and timeline? If feasible, please mark sensitive attachments as "for security review only."

Thanks,
Elena Marsh
Security Program Manager
Phlex Health

Attachment: none (we'll accept your package via Drive or DocuSign link)

From: monica.patel@redwood.com
To: Elena Marsh <elena.marsh@phlexhealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-02T13:05:00Z
Subject: Re: SIG-lite request: subprocessor lineage + short evidence set

Elena —

Appreciate the clear ask. We can deliver a curated evidence pack by May 5 to give you a day for internal review. Plan:

- redwood_subprocessors_20270502.csv: authoritative roster (two-hop transitive column included)
- sig-lite-evidence-index-2027.pdf: mapping SIG-lite control IDs -> artifacts (SOC 2 sections, network diagrams, KMS residency note)
- kms-residency-summary.txt: short summary of KMS boundaries and customer key handling

A few clarifying questions so we scope correctly:
1) Do you want secrets handling (ephemeral tokens, key rotation cadence) included in the CSV or the KMS text? We can do both but would prefer secrets detail in kms-residency-summary.txt.
2) For on-prem connectors: are you only interested in connectors that touch PHI?

Rishi (copied) will attach the KMS residency snippet and confirm whether any subprocessors are using HSM/KMS that we treat as segregated. Laura is looping in Compliance for a quick attestation cover note.

I will place the ZIP on a shared Drive link and send the DocuSign envelope for attestations the same day. Let me know if you need a separate redacted pack for procurement.

Best,
Monica Patel
Manager, Trust & Risk
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_20270502.csv (stub), sig-lite-evidence-index-2027.pdf (stub)

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
To: Elena Marsh <elena.marsh@phlexhealth.com>, monica.patel@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-03T10:48:00Z
Subject: Re: SIG-lite request: subprocessor lineage + short evidence set

Elena / Monica — quick technical note to include in the pack (paste below will go into kms-residency-summary.txt):

--- begin excerpt ---
KMS and customer key handling (summary):
- Customer-managed keys: Redwood supports customer-provided keys via our KMS integration (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). When configured, ciphertext for customer data is encrypted using a customer CMK; Redwood does not persist plaintext customer key material.
- Ephemeral inference tokens: The serving runtime issues short-lived tokens scoped to a single inference session; tokens are rotated every 15 minutes by default.
- HSM usage: Our certificate signing and hardware-backed key material for node attestation may be stored in HSM (AWS CloudHSM) in us-east-1. If a customer requires on-prem HSM, we provide a private deployment package with determinable key residency.
- Transitive processors: listed in CSV under col "transitive_hops"; we enumerated up to two hops (direct partner -> their subprocessor).
--- end excerpt ---

Also note: two subprocessors (EdgeCacheCo and TelemetryOps) do transient logging; both have SOC 2 Type II reports on file — we will include the report names and redacted timestamps in the index.

If you want the technical PKI diagram included, say the word and I'll attach a small PNG.

-Rishi
Principal Applied Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: kms-residency-summary.txt (stub)

From: Elena Marsh <elena.marsh@phlexhealth.com>
To: monica.patel@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: procure@phlexhealth.com, security@phlexhealth.com
Date: 2027-05-04T08:22:00Z

Monica / Rishi — thank you, this is great and on the timeline. A couple of small next steps from our side:

- Procurement prefers a redacted pack for vendor review and a full pack for security only; please mark the Drive folder with those two subfolders.
- Can you add a one-line statement that EdgeCacheCo's logs are ephemeral and are not used for model training?
- We'll accept the DocuSign envelope for the attestation cover note; please send that link when available.

If you can drop the Drive link and the DocuSign link, we'll circulate internally and aim to finalize vendor approval on May 11.

Thanks,
Elena
Security Program Manager
Phlex Health
